content.title: About
content.content: Onion (Allium cepa) is a widely cultivated vegetable bulb used globally as a fundamental aromatic building block in culinary traditions. Available in yellow, red, and white varieties, onions offer a spectrum of flavors from sweet and mild to sharp and pungent.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onions release lachrymatory factor gas when cut, which stimulates eye tear glands.
Yellow onions account for the majority of commercial production worldwide.
Caramelizing onions low and slow converts harsh sulfur compounds into rich sugars.
Ancient Egyptians worshipped onions, viewing their concentric rings as a symbol of eternal life.
Onions are rich in quercetin, a versatile antioxidant bioflavonoid.

items.title: Rich in Quercetin
items.content: A potent antioxidant bioflavonoid that supports cardiovascular health.

items.title: Prebiotic Fiber
items.content: Contains inulin and fructooligosaccharides that feed beneficial gut microbes.

items.title: Antibacterial Action
items.content: Sulfur compounds demonstrate natural antimicrobial properties.

items.title: Bone Density Support
items.content: Regular consumption has been associated with improved bone mineral density in studies.

items.title: FODMAP Sensitivity
items.content: High in fructans, which may cause gas, bloating, and IBS symptoms in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Acid Reflux
items.content: Raw onions can trigger heartburn or acid reflux symptoms.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dice raw for salsas and salads, caramelize slowly for soups and burgers, or roast whole as a flavorful side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unpeeled onions in a cool, dry, dark, well-ventilated space separated from potatoes. Refrigerate cut onions in a sealed container.
